title: How Much Should a Contractor Spend on Marketing? (2026)
h1: How Much Should a Contractor Spend on Marketing?
meta: How much should a contractor spend on marketing? The honest answer isn't a flat percent — it's cost per booked job. Here's how to set a budget that pays.
short: The common rule is 5–10% of revenue, but that's the wrong frame. Budget by cost per booked job: spend where a customer costs less than the job is worth, starting with the free channels you already own.
statLabel: Of revenue is the common rule — but cost per booked job is the number that matters

body.h2: The percent rule is a starting point, not the answer
body.answer: Budget by cost per booked job, not a flat percent.
body.html: Most guides say 5–10% of revenue. Fine as a ceiling — but it tells you nothing about whether a dollar works. The real question: does a channel book jobs for less than the job is worth? Angi ~$542/booked job vs Google LSA ~$168 answers that fast.

body.h2: Start with the channels you already own
body.answer: Free channels first — they have the best return.
body.html: A complete Google Business Profile, steady reviews (91% won't consider under 4 stars — BrightLocal 2026), and a referral system cost almost nothing per lead. Max these before paying for anything.

body.h2: Then add paid where the math works
body.answer: Pay per booked job, not per lead.
body.html: Google Local Service Ads (~$168/booked job, pay per lead) is usually the first paid dollar. Track spend ÷ jobs booked per channel monthly; kill what loses, feed what wins. And answer fast — 78% hire the first responder (Lead Connect 2026).

faq.q: How much should a small contractor spend on marketing?
faq.a: A common rule is 5–10% of revenue, but budget by cost per booked job instead. Max your free/owned channels first, then add paid where a customer costs less than the job is worth (e.g. Google LSA ~$168/booked job).

faq.q: What's a good cost per lead for a contractor?
faq.a: Cost per lead is the wrong metric — it hides your close rate. Track cost per booked job: ~$542 via Angi vs ~$168 via Google LSA once close rates are counted.

faq.q: Where should a contractor spend first?
faq.a: Free/owned channels — Google Business Profile, reviews, referrals — then Google Local Service Ads. Answer every lead fast; 78% hire whoever responds first (Lead Connect 2026).
